# Today in Indian News

Headline summary: Major blaze in Mumbai's electronics hub and high-profile legal, economic and governance developments dominate today's headlines.

- Massive fire at Mumbai's Saraswati Bhavan (Lamington Road): A large blaze reportedly gutted a mobile-phone and accessories warehouse in Mumbai's electronics district; emergency response and damage assessment were ongoing. (Source: The Indian Express live updates) https://indianexpress.com/article/india/today-india-breaking-news-live-updates-6-september-2026-mumbai-saraswati-bhavan-fire-jharkhand-minister-iran-isro-10865238

- CBI names Subhash Chandra in alleged Rs 1,322 crore LIC Housing Finance fraud: The Central Bureau of Investigation has reportedly booked media entrepreneur Subhash Chandra in a high-value alleged fraud linked to LIC Housing Finance, a development that may have legal and business implications. (Source: The Indian Express) https://indianexpress.com/archive/2026/09/06

- Rural jobs show a rise in September: Data reported by The Hindu indicates an increase in employment in rural India in September, a positive signal for household income and consumption ahead of festival season. (Source: The Hindu data piece) https://www.thehindu.com/data/data-jobs-increase-in-rural-india-in-september/article36917306.ece

- IISER Mohali withdraws revised admission by-laws after student objections: The institute reportedly pulled back newly introduced by-laws following protests from students, highlighting governance and student-representation concerns in higher education. (Source: The Indian Express archive) https://indianexpress.com/archive/2026/09/06

- Allegations of police flogging in Gujarat: Local reports say a murder suspect was tied and publicly beaten by police officers, raising questions about police conduct and accountability; details are being reported by regional outlets. (Source: The Indian Express archive) https://indianexpress.com/archive/2026/09/06/page/3

- RBI to conduct 30-day VRRR auction to absorb excess liquidity (reported by Reuters): The central bank is reported to plan a variable-rate reverse repo to allow banks to park surplus funds while keeping withdrawal flexibility, affecting short-term market liquidity. (Source: Reuters India coverage) https://www.reuters.com/world/india
